First, let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14255329/assets/2373daf4b5fd26f098bf90e998e2685db6a8b793e94ac9d80b08ea423cb535c0.png)

From the graph, we note the following:

- The period of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$

- Our graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. This means that $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is an *even* function, and we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Let's now evaluate our expression:

- Firstly, using the periodicity of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x+24\pi ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x+2\pi \cdot 12) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x).\end{aligned}
$$

- Secondly, using the evenness of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x+24\pi )=-1.$
